stem: Why is bilateral nasal obstruction life-threatening in neonates?

options.text: They have an underdeveloped cough reflex
They cannot regulate their oxygen saturation levels

explanation: Newborns must breathe through their nose to survive; if both passages are blocked, they experience severe respiratory distress.
rationale: Consider the specific physiological breathing requirement unique to newborns.

optionExplanations.A: While true, the immediate life threat stems from their inability to switch to mouth breathing efficiently.
optionExplanations.B: Newborns must breathe through their nose to survive; if both passages are blocked, they experience severe respiratory distress.
optionExplanations.C: Oxygen regulation depends on airway patency, which is compromised due to their anatomical reliance on nasal passages.
optionExplanations.D: The danger lies in the upper airway obstruction at the level of the nose, regardless of the size of the lower airway.

source.hint: Consider the specific physiological breathing requirement unique to newborns.
